set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific rule found. The source (Fairfield 2023-2031 Housing Element review draft, Chapter 5 fee discussion) describes the Fee Deferral Program (Municipal Code Ch. 5, Art. I), Fee Credit Bank and Train Station Specific Plan fee reduction but says nothing on prevailing wage. Under Labor Code 1720(b)(4) fees reduced, waived or forgiven by a city are public funds; an interest-free deferral may also count. Coverage then depends on 1720(c) facts: (c)(3) de minimis test (subsidy under $600,000 and under 2 percent of total project cost) and (c)(5) affordable housing exemptions. Outcome depends on project facts, so left unclear (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720).
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; only basis is the general Labor Code 1720(b)(4) public-funds definition, and coverage turns on the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test and 1720(c)(5) exemptions for the specific project. Note: layering_notes cites 1720(c) for public funds; the operative definition is 1720(b)(4).
